components.institution_label: Temporary Change in Duties for Full-Time Teaching Faculty Who Expect a New Family Member through Birth or Adoption
components.description: Full-time (ten-month) teaching faculty expecting a birth or adoption may request one semester (fall, spring or summer) with no teaching, assigned non-teaching duties (research, advising, other) with pay; final approval by the provost. Available from the first year of employment.
components.faculty_group_note: full-time teaching faculty; "ten-month teaching faculty" (university-wide faculty handbook policy)
components.eligible_parent_wording: teaching faculty who expect a new family member through birth or adoption; "both parents"
components.entitlement_note: V2: faculty are 'eligible to request' the change, and the request goes through chair and dean recommendations to the provost 'for final approval'; the approval decides whether the relief is given, not merely its arrangements. Borderline with V2's 'is eligible for' (guaranteed_on_request); flagged.
components.duration_note: 'a maximum of one semester'; the semester may be fall, spring or summer.
components.duration_variants: summer option for ten-month faculty: pay equivalent to a three-credit course, if the member has regularly taught in summer
components.relief_note: Teaching is the duty released; the member is assigned 'non-teaching duties' such as research and advising. Service and clinical duties are not named and are coded continues (R4b). Category: Just teaching.
components.service_requirement: none stated; available in the first year of employment regardless of hours worked
components.dual_employee_rule: both parents in the same department must propose staggered periods
components.notice: written request to the department chair, as soon as practicable

components.description: University Policy 6050: up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a rolling 12-month period for the birth of a child, adoption or foster placement, care of a spouse, child or parent with a serious health condition, or the employee's own serious health condition; accrued paid leave runs concurrently; intermittent or reduced-schedule leave with supervisor approval.

components.description: BOV Policy 1430: sick leave with pay, granted when necessary during the contract period, continuing until the member can resume duties but for no longer than six months of sick leave per contract period; the period before, during and after delivery certified by the physician as medically necessary may be charged to it; any further absence is without pay.
components.mechanism_note: V1: the policy names pregnancy and childbirth but states no childbirth-specific period or default length (the physician-certified period is the measure), so it stays a generic plan. R1: a fixed paid allotment the employer grants each contract period (not days earned and carried over), so an employer plan, not own_accrual. U6: the text charges certified absences to sick leave (pay applied to absences), it does not grant a leave status of stated length, so no separate leave component.
components.faculty_group_note: "faculty members or administrative and professional faculty (AP faculty)"; 'teaching and research faculty'
components.eligible_parent_wording: recuperation due to pregnancy or childbirth; "the mother's health condition related to childbirth"
components.duration_note: Plan maximum: 'no longer than six months of sick leave during those months normally covered by contract'. No childbirth period is stated; the childbirth use is the physician-certified period (V6: plan's short-term entitlement).
components.medical_certification_note: period of absence 'certified by a physician as medically necessary'

sequence.note: BOV 1430: FMLA applies to absences for the birth or the mother's childbirth-related health condition; sick pay runs alongside the FMLA leave (not within it, since the plan can run up to six months).

mechanism: Faculty or AP faculty may use sick leave with pay for the period of absence that is certified by a physician as medically necessary because of illness, health conditions, or recuperation due to pregnancy or childbirth.
the period of absence before, during and after delivery that is certified by the attending physician as medically necessary may be charged to sick leave.
faculty_group: It is the policy of the university to grant sick leave with pay to faculty members or administrative and professional faculty (AP faculty) when this becomes necessary during the period covered by the person's contract.
eligible_parent: Faculty or AP faculty may use sick leave with pay for the period of absence that is certified by a physician as medically necessary because of illness, health conditions, or recuperation due to pregnancy or childbirth.
entitlement: It is the policy of the university to grant sick leave with pay to faculty members or administrative and professional faculty (AP faculty) when this becomes necessary during the period covered by the person's contract.

notes: Reference date 2018-01-01. First coded in January 2019 (2019-01-29), after the 2017-18 academic year; DHRM Policy 4.21 (c10), effective 2018-06-26, is flagged not_yet_effective (V5) and enters no value.

Many handbook sections are only links to policies that are not saved (e.g. BOV 1491 Annual Leave for 12-month faculty, BOV 1431 Military, 1433 Civil and Administrative, 1434 Bone Marrow and Organ Donor, 1435 Emergency/Disaster, 1436 Recognition, 1437 School Assistance and Volunteer Service Leave, University Policy 6052 Lactation Support, 5406 Accommodations for Individuals with Disabilities, 6702 Children in the Workplace, the ODU benefits page for ODU Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability and Aflac, and the VSDP Guidebook).

BOV Policy 1411 (Tenure): the handbook (2018_00) prints the June 9, 2016 version, in force on the reference date; the revision effective July 1, 2018 (agenda book 2018_05, adopted per the minutes 2018_06) leaves III.B.4 and III.C unchanged in substance, so c8-c9 hold under both. The agenda copy is a redline (deleted and inserted words run together); quotes are taken from unchanged passages.

Path by retirement-plan election (U8, checklist §1): faculty who elected the Virginia Retirement System are enrolled in the Virginia Sickness and Disability Program (handbook pp. 210): 8-10 days of sick leave and 4-5 days of family and personal leave a year; short-term disability after a seven-calendar-day wait, 100/80/60% of income for up to 125 workdays depending on state service (60% for fewer than five years; employees hired on or after July 1, 2009 have a one-year waiting period and a different, unstated schedule); long-term disability after 180 calendar days at 60%. The coded path is BOV 1430 sick leave (up to six months with pay per contract period), the Board's faculty sick-leave policy that the parental Temporary Change in Duties policy refers to; VSDP is not coded as a component and the two are not linked in_lieu_of. Flagged on c3 as a rule gap.

DHRM Policy 4.21 (8 weeks paid parental leave, effective 2018-06-26) took effect after the reference date (c10, flagged not_yet_effective) and in any case covers only positions under the Virginia Personnel Act; teaching and research staff are exempt (Va. Code 2.2-2905(8), saved statute). Coded as c10 with a named group, so it counts in no faculty figure. No ODU policy extending paid parental leave to teaching and research faculty is among the saved sources.

BOV 1430 also says any absence beyond the physician-certified period 'must be taken as leave without pay'; no length is stated, so that unpaid time is covered by FMLA (c2) and no separate component is coded.

Calendar: the handbook's accelerated-course policy states 'traditional semester credit courses of 15 weeks of instruction during the fall and spring semesters'; coded term_weeks 15 (R8). This is instruction weeks; the semester also has a final-examination period.

Chain, birth parent: one semester with no teaching (c1, discretionary, Just teaching) in the semester of the birth, with FMLA 12 weeks (c2) concurrent from its start and BOV 1430 sick leave with pay for the physician-certified period (c3, generic plan, up to six months) concurrent with FMLA; LTD (c5, employee-paid) only after six months of sick leave.
Chain, non-birth parent: one semester with no teaching (c1, discretionary) with FMLA 12 weeks (c2) concurrent from its start; family-illness sick leave (c4, 10 days, general purpose) not placed.
Guaranteed paid leave for tenure-stream faculty after a birth: none dedicated; the only parental relief (c1) requires provost approval (coded discretionary, flagged).
